text.p: Homestake Mining Co plans to grow by continuing its accelerated exploration program and maintaining aggressive pursuit of acquisitions, chief executive Jack Thompson said Wednesday.
"Homestake plans to grow by fulfilling three key initiatives," he told the European Gold Mining Investment Forum in Geneva, Switzerland.

"First, we will continue our strong support for exploration, spending around $45 to 50 million in 1997. It is during periods of low gold prices that opportunities are most abundant and exploration properties more easily acquired.
"Our goal is to maximize the probability of finding and developing large, low-cost mines," Thompson said.

"Second, we will maintain our aggressive pursuit of acquisitions that we believe will create value for our shareholders. Any acquisitions we make will be consistent with our objective to build a larger, more profitable company.
"Our recent bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold, although not successful, is an example of this commitment.
"Third, Homestake will continue to strive to improve performance at its existing operations to achieve maximum production, lower costs and increased profitability."
Thompson commented that Homestake's accelerated exploration program has resulted in two new discoveries in the last three years.

The Ruby Hill mine near Eureka, Nev., will be in production in the fourth quarter of 1997 and will be the company's lowest cost operation. Furthermore, deep drilling has indicated a major gold system some 1,500 feet below the planned West Archimedes open pit. If these promising results continued, development of an underground mine at Ruby Hill in the future would be a distinct possibility, he said.

At the Jeronimo/Agua de la Falda project in Chile, Homestake has outlined mineralized material and reserves in excess of two million ounces of gold to date. Production has started on the oxide portion of the deposit while the company evaluates the potential of the deeper sulfide portion of the mineralization.

While much work remains to be done to determine the economics of the sulfide portion of the mineralization, recent drilling has provided some of the best results to date, Thompson said. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
